{{Field procedure|summary=Travel to a mapped ring hotspot, drop into the ring safely, and begin prospecting inside the target area.}}

Use this procedure after a [[Planetary Rings|planetary ring]] has been mapped and the commander wants to start a mining run inside a visible [[Mining Hotspot|mining hotspot]].

{{Draft warning}}

== Before you start ==

* Complete [[How to Scan Planetary Rings for Mining Hotspots]] or obtain a known hotspot location.
* Fit the mining equipment for the chosen method.
* Bring limpets if the build uses a [[Prospector Limpet Controller]] or [[Collector Limpet Controller]].
* Confirm the ship has cargo space after loading limpets.

== Procedure ==

{{Procedure steps|
# Select the hotspot marker in the navigation panel or directly from the ring display.
# Approach the marker in supercruise and reduce speed early enough to avoid an unsafe drop.
# Drop into the ring near the hotspot marker, not into the planet or exclusion zone.
# Let the ship settle, check contacts, and avoid boosting through dense asteroid traffic.
# Move away from the arrival point before starting sustained mining activity.
# Fire a prospector limpet at candidate asteroids or begin the method-specific search pattern.
# Continue only if the asteroid contents, deposits, or core signals match the run's goal.
}}

== Completion check ==

The procedure is complete when the ship is safely inside the hotspot area and the commander has begun prospecting or searching asteroids for the selected mining method.

== Common problems ==

* '''The ship drops far from the marker:''' approach again in supercruise and watch speed and distance before dropping.
* '''Asteroids do not contain the target commodity:''' a hotspot increases targeting usefulness but does not make every asteroid valuable.
* '''Limpets run out early:''' leave the ring before the run becomes inefficient; limpets are the ammunition for prospecting and collection.
* '''Hostile ships appear:''' be ready to leave, especially if carrying valuable refined cargo.
